Hi Alicia 

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers while I sync up with infra: 

1) Hosted API behavior during spikes: our control plane does workload-aware routing across zones and model variants. For large, bursty customers we have automatic overflow rules that route to compatible model variants or to reserved Dedicated pools if configured via policy. That reduces the chance of a single shared pool causing 95th pct latency breaches. However, Hosted customers do share physical resources, so absolute isolation guarantees are limited compared to Dedicated.

2) Dedicated guarantees: when you purchase a Dedicated pool we provide tenant-level GPU reservations (dedicated vGPUs per customer) and network isolation within the cluster. Noisy neighbor effects within a tenant are eliminated because other customers do not share those GPUs. Our SLA for Dedicated covers availability (monthly uptime) and per-instance performance baselines; we can add an addendum that defines isolation expectations for latency SLOs during your payroll windows.

3) Logs/export: yes  workspace-level audit logs and per-token traces can be exported to your Splunk/S3/SIEM. We'll provide the export config and retention options for compliance review.

4) Lead time for Dedicated: standard lead time for initial Dedicated capacity is 6–8 weeks from PO (could be shorter with existing pre-warmed pools or by using a hybrid approach: short-term Hosted with strict routing policies + Dedicated for steady-state).

I'll attach a short FAQ and example SLA clause. Vivek  can you confirm the isolation addendum language we should propose to procurement?
—Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Shared vs Dedicated: noisy neighbor follow-up - FinPay RFP

Hi Alicia 

Quick technical note from infra as requested: 

- Isolation model for Dedicated: Dedicated pools are provisioned as tenant-isolated namespaces. GPUs are exclusively attached to tenant instances (no multi-tenant GPU sharing). Network isolation is enforced via private subnets and at-rest/encryption-in-transit controls per your KMS.
- Latency SLOs: we can contract a 95th percentile per-request latency target and define measurement windows tied to your payroll events. We recommend a short ramp-and-validate period (2 weeks of production traffic) to lock in the final thresholds.
- Noisy neighbor mitigation in Hosted: our runtime uses continuous batching and adaptive kernel selection; during bursts we throttle background batching for non-priority customers and route high-priority traffic to warmed instances. That said, if you require absolute per-tenant isolation during payroll spikes, Dedicated is the correct fit.
- Operational runbook: we will provide a canary plan, warm-start checklist, and an escalation path (priority on-call + 15-min response SLA for critical incidents) as part of the Dedicated onboarding.

Next steps I propose:
1) We draft a one-paragraph isolation addendum for the SOW stating GPU exclusivity, private subnets, and a 95th latency target measurement method.
2) Schedule a 30-min procurement + infra call to review addendum and lead times.

Marissa  if you can share a few time slots Ill block the calendar. Alicia  earliest availability from your side?

Thanks 
Vivek
